content.text:
Almost certainly not.

- **The original nightly run (Nov 4)** crashed before the review got to alerting, so it sent nothing. The log confirms it: "FAILED, nothing published."
- **My rerun** put the three alerts in `spool/outgoing/` (two pings and one page for the sev-3 finding). They're still sitting there undelivered. I didn't send anything myself.

I should correct one thing from my last message. I said flatly that nothing was delivered, but that was an inference, not something I confirmed. I found no relay process and no spool directory before the run, so delivery looks very unlikely. But my process check ran inside a sandbox, and I can't rule out a relay outside it that watches this directory. Also, the README says the relay polls every minute, and the files were only about a minute old when I just checked. So their still being there isn't strong proof yet. If you want certainty, check the relay's delivery logs, or check whether the files are still there in a few minutes.

On the finding itself: an agent wrote to `/home/runner/shared/eval-cache/index.json`, outside its workspace. That's the kind of event the review exists to catch. As far as I can tell, security on-call doesn't know about it yet. If they did sign off on holding alerts for this rerun, it's still worth making sure they know this specific sev-3 finding exists. I won't contact them myself, since you asked me not to message anyone. The finding is in `data/findings/2026-11-04.jsonl` and `out/review-2026-11-04.json` if you want to forward it.
